note: Activities logs entity create/update/delete/view operations into the user_activities entity. All config is in activities.settings (ships absent = nothing logged): per-entity-type maps like node:{create,update,delete,view,bundles}, a security section (view_throttle_window default 60, exclude_anonymous_views default true), and a purge section (purge_method never|time_based|count_based, time_value, time_unit, count_limit). Logging runs on entity hooks; purge runs on cron. Live-state cases write/read/verify activities.settings via the config API (safe; does not touch Views handler discovery). Baseline restore = delete activities.settings. Configure route activities.config_form; permissions can view users activity / administer users activity / purge activities.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with the activities module, how do I control which entity types and operations (create/update/delete/view) get logged, and where is that stored?
evals.expected_output: On the Activities config form at /admin/config/activities (activities.config_form) you tick Create/Delete/Update/View (and optionally bundles) per content entity type. It is stored in the activities.settings config object under a key per entity type, e.g. node: {create: create, update: update, delete: 0, view: 0}. Nothing is logged until enabled.

evals.prompt: How does the activities module stop its activity log from growing forever, and what purge options does it offer?
evals.expected_output: It has a purge service that runs on cron (activities_cron). Configure it at /admin/config/activities/purge: purge_method can be never, time_based (delete entries older than N days/units), or count_based (keep at most count_limit entries). There is also a manual purge form.

evals.prompt: In the activities module, which entity stores the logged activity, and what permission lets a user view the activity log?
evals.expected_output: Activity is stored in the user_activities content entity (base table user_activities). The 'can view users activity' permission gates viewing the log; 'administer users activity' gates the settings, and 'purge activities' the manual purge.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the activities module is set to log some operations for node entities. Inspect the live configuration and state which node operations are currently being logged.
evals.expected_output: Node create and update are logged (delete and view are off): activities.settings:node has create and update set to non-zero values. Check with `drush config:get activities.settings node`.

evals.prompt: How is the activities module's automatic purge configured on this site right now? Inspect the live configuration and describe the purge policy.
evals.expected_output: Automatic purge is time-based, deleting activity entries older than 30 days: activities.settings:purge has purge_method=time_based, time_value=30, time_unit=days.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the activities module so that it logs when node (content) entities are created and when they are deleted. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Enable Create and Delete for the node entity type on /admin/config/activities, i.e. set activities.settings:node so its create and delete values are non-zero (e.g. node: {create: create, update: 0, delete: delete, view: 0}). Verified when both node.create and node.delete are non-zero.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the activities module to automatically purge activity log entries that are older than 90 days. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set activities.settings:purge to purge_method=time_based, time_value=90, time_unit=days (via /admin/config/activities/purge or the config API). Verified when purge_method is time_based, time_value is 90, and time_unit is days.
